title: Sackhickneyah Creek
summary: Sackhickneyah is recorded as a creek in northern Newtown, Queens County, near Fish's Point.
history_content: The creek rose in Trains meadow and emptied into Flushing Bay. A 1666 deed named it as the creek where Wessel's mill stood.
translation_content:
Sackhickneyah is interpreted as probably Algonquian despite its Iroquoian appearance, with comparison to a Delaware form meaning "the shore path."

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names and physical objects such as public sites, monuments, and buildings provide access to intricate aspects of history, memory, and place.”

— Stephan Fuchs, History and heritage of two Midwestern towns: a toponymic-material approach (2015), Abstract
preservation_content: Sackhickneyah preserves a Native place-name in the heavily changed shoreline of northern Queens. The name connects Flushing Bay with older paths, meadows, and mill records in Newtown.
